solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Where designs are cooked up, even meals (7,5)

blocks.note: drawing = levelling the score, making things even
board = meals provided, as in bed and board

annotation.surface: A kitchen scene where plans and dinners are both being cooked up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cooked up' and 'meals' pull towards the kitchen, but the definition means devised: a drawing board is where designs are first sketched.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: plans still being devised are said to be at this stage, from the board draughtsmen sketch on.

entries.clue: Quiet going to one’s bedroom? (8)

blocks.note: quiet in the sense of shy and reserved
to retire is to go to bed

annotation.surface: Someone slipping off quietly to bed.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses sit in the same picture, so the clue reads as one idea rather than two definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are plain: a shy, reserved person is described this way, and going off to bed is the same word as a verb.

entries.clue: Insect that’s small seized by hand from below (4)

indicatorNotes.seized by: the hand grips S, so S goes inside
indicatorNotes.from below: in a down clue, reading from below turns the word upside down

blocks.note: a paw is an animal's hand
S = small, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A tiny insect caught in someone's hand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hand' looks human, but crosswords often use an animal's paw for it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain example: the yellow-and-black stinging species is one kind of insect.

entries.clue: Purchasing method on no account repeated (5-5)

indicatorNotes.repeated: something repeated is said a second time, so the same word follows itself

annotation.surface: A shopper swearing never to buy that way again.
annotation.walkthrough: The never-never is British slang for hire purchase, buying goods by instalments, the joke being that you never finish paying.
annotation.definitionFit: Buying on the never-never is a way of purchasing on credit.

entries.clue: Head of giant squeezed in morphing of a blue whale (6)

indicatorNotes.squeezed in: G is pressed inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.morphing of: morphing changes shape, so A BLUE is rearranged

blocks.note: first letter of giant, placed between U and A

annotation.surface: A giant blue whale changing shape.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blue whale' reads as one animal, but it splits: 'a blue' is fodder and 'whale' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The beluga is a small white Arctic whale.

entries.clue: Daughter taken into theatre with onset of lurgy – glandular? (7)

indicatorNotes.taken into: a thing taken into a place ends up inside it, so D goes within the theatre
indicatorNotes.onset of: an onset is a beginning, so only the opening letter of lurgy is used

blocks.note: an arena is a theatre of action
D = daughter, as in family trees

annotation.surface: A daughter taken to the operating theatre with a mysterious bug that might be glandular fever.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests a hospital operating theatre, but it is ARENA; the lurgy is British slang for any unnamed illness.
annotation.definitionFit: The adrenal glands sit on the kidneys, so adrenal means relating to a gland.

entries.clue: A bond allowed to be redrafted – as online files may be (12)

indicatorNotes.redrafted: a redraft rewrites the letters in a new order

annotation.surface: A legal bond being rewritten so it can be shared online.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bond' and 'redrafted' suggest legal paperwork, which hides a long anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: Files online are often downloadable, able to be copied to your own device.

entries.clue: Northern parts behind French city (6)

indicatorNotes.parts: N parts, or splits, the word for the behind

blocks.note: nates = the buttocks, a Latin anatomical word

annotation.surface: Some northern districts lying behind a French city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parts behind' reads as a noun phrase about districts; in fact 'parts' is a verb and 'behind' is the buttocks.
annotation.definitionFit: Nantes is a city in western France on the Loire.

entries.clue: Agreement with no room for manoeuvre dictated (4)

indicatorNotes.dictated: dictated words are spoken, so we go by sound

blocks.note: packed = full, with no room to move

annotation.surface: A deal imposed with no room for negotiation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No room for manoeuvre dictated' reads as a hardline negotiator's terms, but the room is literal space.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a treaty or deal between two parties is an agreement.

entries.clue: Broadcast featuring a more wretched London street (6,3)

indicatorNotes.featuring: a show featuring someone has them in it, so SOW holds the other letters

blocks.note: to sow seed is to broadcast it

annotation.surface: A programme about a grim London street.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests radio or television, but it means scattering seed. SAVILE ROW is the London street famous for tailors.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this Mayfair street, famous for bespoke tailoring, is one of London's streets.

entries.clue: Pure – as a whistle at a high pitch? (7,5)

annotation.definition2: as a whistle at a high pitch

blocks.note: pure in the sense of spotless, beyond reproach

blocks.clueFragment: as a whistle at a high pitch
blocks.note: 'clean as a whistle', and a high-pitched whistle is squeaky

annotation.surface: Someone as pure as a shrill whistle.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half plays on the saying 'clean as a whistle': a whistle at a high pitch is squeaky, giving squeaky clean.
annotation.definitionFit: Squeaky clean means completely pure or above reproach.

entries.clue: Asian cheers having invaded country to the west (6)

indicatorNotes.to the west: in an across clue, going west is right to left

annotation.surface: Asians cheering after invading a western country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' reads as a celebration, but in British speech it also means thanks, the same as ta.
annotation.definitionFit: A Qatari comes from Qatar, in Asia.

entries.clue: First Test, with one catcher brought in (8)

indicatorNotes.brought in: players brought in join the side, so I and GIN are brought inside ORAL

blocks.note: an oral is a spoken exam
a gin is a snare or trap

annotation.surface: A cricket report on the first Test match, with a new wicketkeeper brought into the side.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First Test' and 'catcher' conjure cricket, where a Test is an international match; here the test is an exam and the catcher is a trap.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the first version of something, the one all copies come from, is this.

entries.clue: Where one would compete for food, belly needing a bit, fed nothing (6,4)

annotation.definition: Where one would compete for food

indicatorNotes.fed: food that is fed goes into a mouth, so O goes inside TRACE

blocks.note: a pot, or pot belly, is a paunch

annotation.surface: A hungry belly wanting a bite after being given nothing to eat.
annotation.walkthrough: Belly, food and fed make it all about eating, but the food is the potato that runners carry in a sports-day race.
annotation.definitionFit: A potato race is a children's race in which competitors collect potatoes, so one competes for food.

entries.clue: President in here, so we gathered (10)

indicatorNotes.gathered: the letters are gathered up and rearranged

annotation.surface: An announcement that the president is in the room, so everyone has assembled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gathered' reads as the crowd assembling for the President, which disguises its job.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Dwight D., the 34th US leader and wartime general, held the office.

entries.clue: Insect has run off when picked up? (4)

indicatorNotes.when picked up: picked up means heard, so we go by sound

annotation.surface: A bug scuttling away when someone tries to pick it up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' fits an insect lifted by hand, but it means heard.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the tiny wingless jumper that bites pets is an insect.

entries.clue: Primitive mood in shade of green (5-3)

indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another sits inside it, so the mood goes within the green

blocks.note: the tone of a piece is its mood

annotation.surface: A primitive mood painted in a green colour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shade' suggests colour, and it is one, but 'mood' is the word that goes inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Stone-age means extremely primitive or outdated.

entries.clue: Live on floor in Japanese city (4)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, BE comes on, or after, KO

blocks.note: to floor someone is to knock them out, KO

annotation.surface: Living on a particular floor of a building in a Japanese city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Floor' looks like a storey of a flat, but it is a verb: a boxer floored is knocked out.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the port on Osaka Bay, known for its beef, is a Japanese city.

entries.clue: Panic on high street, rely on career (4,3)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, BANK sits on top of RUN

blocks.note: to bank on = to rely on
to career is to rush along, run

annotation.surface: A shopper in a panic on the high street, counting on a career.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun about jobs; it is the verb to hurtle. A high street is a town's main shopping street, where the banks are.
annotation.definitionFit: A bank run is a panic in which depositors rush to withdraw money from high-street banks.

entries.clue: Iran bamboozled by most sickly Italian scorer (10)

indicatorNotes.bamboozled: bamboozled means confused, so IRAN is rearranged

annotation.surface: An ill Italian footballer getting the better of Iran.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' suggests a goal-scorer, but it means a composer who writes scores: Palestrina wrote Renaissance church music.
annotation.definitionFit: Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina was an Italian composer, a writer of musical scores.

entries.clue: Hot tea for felon (6)

blocks.note: maté is a South American herbal tea

annotation.surface: A hot cup of tea made for a prisoner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hot tea' reads as a drink, but hot means trendy and the tea is maté, the South American infusion.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: a convicted felon ends up locked in prison, where every resident goes by this word.

entries.clue: Wally in form in the end, winning on favourite (6)

indicatorNotes.in the end: only the final letter of form is used

blocks.note: the teacher's pet is a favourite

annotation.surface: A fool who, on form at last, backed the favourite and won.
annotation.walkthrough: The racing words (form, favourite, winning) hide the answer; wally and muppet are both British slang for a fool.
annotation.definitionFit: A muppet, like a wally, is a British term for a foolish person.

entries.clue: Trick panellist – one might trick audience (8)

blocks.note: a juror sits on a jury panel

annotation.surface: Someone deceiving a jury, and a performer deceiving a crowd.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Panellist' suggests a game-show guest, but the panel is the jury. The setter uses 'trick' twice on purpose: once as wordplay, once inside the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A conjuror is a magician who tricks the audience with illusions.

entries.clue: Barbarian‘s plate thrown about (6)

indicatorNotes.thrown about: about means turned round, so the word is reversed

blocks.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer

annotation.surface: A barbarian hurling a dinner plate around.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Thrown about' looks like an anagram signal, but no rearranging is needed: LAMINA simply turns round.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a brutish, uncivilised person gets called a beast, the word for any creature.

entries.clue: Drink taken in tavernas, tisane (4)

indicatorNotes.taken in: the answer is held inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the last two letters of tavernas and first two of tisane

annotation.surface: A herbal tea ordered in Greek tavernas.
annotation.walkthrough: The drink is Asti, the Italian sparkling wine, not the tisane the surface offers.
annotation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont.

entries.clue: English person and a Ukrainian initially replaced Frenchman and German, for example (9)

indicatorNotes.initially: only the first letter of Ukrainian
indicatorNotes.replaced: the letters are put back in a new order

annotation.surface: An English person and a Ukrainian standing in for a Frenchman and a German.
annotation.walkthrough: The nationalities in the surface make every word look like a definition; only the last phrase is one.
annotation.definitionFit: The French and Germans are both examples of Europeans.

entries.clue: Unconventional person legally shaving head (4)

indicatorNotes.shaving head: shaving a head removes what is on top, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: in law a party is a person involved in a case or contract; drop the P

annotation.surface: A bohemian lawyer shaving their head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Person legally' is one unit: the legal word for a person in a contract is a party.
annotation.definitionFit: Arty means bohemian or unconventional in style.

entries.clue: Tension where fumbling about still in the dark? (4,3,5)

indicatorNotes.fumbling about: fumbling mixes things up, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: The tension of groping around in the dark.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Where' looks like a link word, but it is fodder, supplying the W, H and two Es.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: having learned nothing from an explanation leaves you as ignorant as before, still in the dark.
